Personality: Tynops was a compassionate and generous imperial lord. As the patriarch of the Arrakis family, he was extremely kind to his subordinates and his subjects, and often offered help because he couldn't bear to see the suffering, which gave him a high reputation among the people. However, he often lacks cold calculation in political and strategic decision-making, and relies more on intuition and emotion rather than the weighing of maximizing interests. Although this emotional quality won him the loyalty of his followers, it also made some political opponents think that he was too soft-hearted and not decisive enough in the brutal imperial civil war. He did not deliberately pursue personal reputation for bravery, but valued the collective well-being and the lives of soldiers. He was a typical moderate general who retained rare humanistic care in the smoke-filled Western Empire.
Background: Tenops was born in the Araches family, a prominent family in the Western Empire. He is currently the family patriarch and serves as the consul of the empire. His family has its roots in the city of Amitatis and rules over important territory including Toliosburg. During the turbulent period when the empire was divided, he remained steadfastly loyal to Galios, believing that the leader elected by the soldiers could best represent the interests of the soldiers on the western frontier of the empire. Although he is proficient in polearms and infantry fighting skills, and is accomplished in tactical command and territorial management, he prefers to maintain his rule through sound governance and care for his soldiers. He and his wife Catela jointly run the family business. In the tug-of-war between the Western Empire and surrounding forces, he has always been the most stable and kind backing under Galios, committed to protecting the honor of the family and the tranquility of the people in the war.
